assertions.name: cosh_sinh_bridge_verified
assertions.source: [n]_q = sinh(nλ)/sinh(λ) verified to 1e-40 for n in {2,3,9,10}.

description: Item 2 of PR #1708: tests whether the sinh (Coulomb) channel of prop:cosh-sinh-q-bridge, through Wedderburn, derives the α_em 2/(3π) shift and [2]_q/(8π)·(1−h²α) self-energy. Confirms tree term + [2]_q numerator are Coulomb-channel; shift coeff and Schwinger factor are not independently derived.

data.verdict:
PARTIAL / INTERPRETIVE. The cosh/sinh bridge is verified ([n]_q = sinh(nλ)/sinh(λ) to 1e-40). The tree term IS a pure Coulomb-channel (sinh) object, confirming the chain `cat action → sinh channel → Wedderburn` produces the LEADING α_em⁻¹. For the CORRECTIONS:
  • The 2/(3π) shift coincides with the STANDARD QED 1-loop vacuum-polarization β-function coefficient (2/3π per charged fermion). The framework's '3' admits a CONSISTENT reading as N_blocks=3 at H_3 (= N_cusps of the Borromean complement), but the value 2/(3π) is the textbook QED result, not a NEW categorical derivation — genuine λ-dependent sinh forms (tanh(λ)/(πλ)-type) do NOT match.
  • The self-energy [2]_q/(8π)·(1−h²α): the [2]_q numerator IS a Coulomb-channel (sinh(2λ)/sinh(λ)) object, but the (1−h²α) Schwinger factor is NOT a pure Coulomb-channel form (cosh⁻² damping misses). This factor is the RT-2-loop track's target.
NET: the Coulomb channel structurally explains the TREE term and the [2]_q numerator of the self-energy, and gives a consistent N_blocks=3 reading of the 2/(3π) shift — but does NOT independently DERIVE the 2/(3π) coefficient or the (1−h²α) factor. Those remain the QED-vacuum-polarization import + the RT-2-loop Schwinger derivation respectively. Consistent with Item 1 (multi-cell summed Yekutieli also could not derive the shift coefficient).
